To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
protein synthetic activity increases in the dendrites of granular cells during early stages of reinnervation of the denervated hippocampus.
the increased protein synthesis is not confined to glial cells or vascular elements, that it occurs in the dendrites of granular cells, and that it is not due to increased precursor transport.
the incorporation of [3H]-leucine is increased in the neuropil of the denervated dentate gyrus, and that the increase is not due to increased availability of the precursor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
cellular mechanisms that may be involved in post-lesion synaptogenic events in the adult brain.
the cellular metabolic events that accompany reinnervation of the hippocampal formation following entorhinal cortical lesions.
the cellular metabolic events which occur in the dentate region following entorhinal lesion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the incorporation of protein precursor is increased in the denervating neuropil of the denervated dentate gyrus of adult rats during the early phase (6-12 days) of reinnervation following unilateral destruction of entorhinal cortical input.
the increased incorporation of protein precursors in the denervate dentate neuropil occurs primarily within the dendrites of granular cells during the early phases of reinnervation.

the increased incorporation of [3H]-leucine in the denervate dentate gyrus of the hippocampus is a reflection of a rapid transport of protein precursors from cell bodies to dendritic terminals and that this increased incorporation is a reflection of increased protein synthesis in the denervating dendrites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the increased protein precursor incorporation in the neuropil of the denervated dentate gyrus occurs primarily within the dendrites of granular cells during the early stages of reactive synaptogenesis, suggesting that protein synthetic activity within these cells may be involved in the reinnervation process.
the increased precursor incorporation in the denervation zone of the neuropil during the early phase is not a direct consequence of the increased protein synthesis in the granule cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the incorporation of [3H]-leucine is increased in the neuropil ipsilateral to the lesion, and the availability of unincorporated [3H] leucine and its degradation products is decreased in the neuropil.

the increased protein precursor incorporation in the neuropil during the early stages of reinnervation is probably not due to an increase in the amount of precursor in the neuropil, but rather to an increase in its rate of incorporation into protein by dendrites of granular cells.
there is a significant increase in the incorporation of leucine into the neuropil in the denervative zone.
